evals.name: show-me-rrf-demo
evals.prompt: show me how the RRF demo works. the file is examples/rrf/demo.py
evals.expected_output: A rendered code-history page plus a short chat answer grounded in the run.
assertions: Recorded the program instead of only reading its source (a run.json exists, or the answer cites step numbers)
Produced a rendered HTML code-history page
Every checkpoint on the page carries a pyokka command that reproduces it
Re-running each checkpoint's verify command reproduces its values exactly
The answer states the actual result, that C finishes first, with its score
The answer cites file:line and step numbers the user can jump to
The answer is written for a person, not pasted CLI output

evals.name: why-contribution-value
evals.prompt: in examples/rrf/demo.py, contribution comes out as 0.015873 on some passes and 0.016393 on others. why? show me where that difference comes from.
evals.expected_output: A rendered code-history page plus a short chat answer grounded in the run.
assertions: Answered from the recording (used why, var or values) rather than doing the arithmetic from the source
Gives the correct cause: the two numbers are 1/(60+3) and 1/(60+1), so the rank differs
Names specific steps where each of the two values occurred
Produced a rendered HTML code-history page
Re-running each checkpoint's verify command reproduces its values exactly

evals.name: cold-explain-ranking-module
evals.prompt: explain how examples/rrf/api/ranking.py actually works when the service uses it. i have not run anything yet.
evals.expected_output: A rendered code-history page plus a short chat answer grounded in the run.
assertions: Made a recording of the module actually running instead of only reading the source
Exercised ranking.py the way the service uses it, not in isolation from the request path
Separates what the run shows from what was not observed, rather than asserting unobserved behaviour
Produced a rendered HTML code-history page
Did not read or print the project's .env

evals.name: live-debug-handler
evals.prompt: the /rank endpoint in examples/rrf/api/main.py is returning documents in the wrong order. pause it in the handler on a real request and show me what it actually received.
evals.expected_output: A rendered code-history page plus a short chat answer grounded in the run.
assertions: Chose the live debugger rather than trying to answer from a recording
Actually paused in the handler and reported the payload the request carried
Labelled the evidence as a live pause, not as a recorded step
Did not claim a provenance chain for a pause that recorded nothing behind it
Stopped the debug session when finished, leaving no paused program holding the port
